name: Table 1-8: Orbital Features
_doc: Roll N times based on Gravity result. Subtables for Rocky Planets vs Gas Giants.

rocky_planets.name: No Features
rocky_planets.description: No notable features are added to the Planet's orbit.

rocky_planets.name: Large Asteroid
rocky_planets.description: An asteroid of unusual size has been captured by the Planet's gravity well, in a stable orbit. Large enough to be noted by an orbital survey, but not seen from the surface without visual enhancement.

rocky_planets.name: Lesser Moon
rocky_planets.description: An orbital body between an extremely large asteroid and a very small moon. Limited gravity well allows low-gravity travel (RT Core p.269). Roll 1d10; on 6+ it counts as a Resource — roll once on Table 1-20: Mineral Resources and once on Table 1-19 (Abundance) at -5.

rocky_planets.name: Moon
rocky_planets.description: A true moon, generated as a Planet (Planet Creation p.19). Normally cannot have a higher Planetary Body than its parent. A moon never generates its own Orbital Features.

gas_giants.name: No Features
gas_giants.description: No notable features added to the Gas Giant's orbit.

gas_giants.name: Planetary Rings (Debris)
gas_giants.description: Narrow band of asteroids/ice. Direct passage requires Challenging (+0) Pilot (Space Craft)+Manoeuvrability as if Asteroid Field (RT Core p.226-227). Multiple instances stack: -10 to passage tests per additional instance.

gas_giants.name: Planetary Rings (Dust)
gas_giants.description: Wide ring of fine particles. Auger tests through the ring are two steps more difficult. Multiple instances increase the existing Rings; -5 additional auger-penalty for every two additional instances.

gas_giants.name: Lesser Moon
gas_giants.description: Roll 1d10; on 6+ houses sufficient mineral wealth to count as a Resource — roll once on Table 1-20 and determine Abundance by rolling 5d10+5.

gas_giants.name: Moon
gas_giants.description: Generated as a Planet (page 19). Cannot have higher Planetary Body than parent. Never generates its own Orbital Features.
